holderQuote: “We have a [Runecrafter]! Try Bezoar Street—go right at the statue of the [Florist]. Ask for Miss Ediya. The old woman with the white hair. She’ll set you up.”

Miss Ediya’s shop was cluttered—mainly with little stones with delicate sigils etched on them. There was very little space for a customer; the counter encircled Fals on three sides. Most of the shop was the [Runecrafter]’s workspace. The old woman was probably in her sixties, but she was quite fit as she bent to one side, grabbing for her desk.
“Don’t run off just yet. It can be recharged. And it will keep you cool! [Runecrafter]’s oath.”
“[Runecrafter], Miss Ediya? I thought there were [Runesmiths].”
“It’s good, Miss Ediya. But a gold piece and three silver is a lot.”
